articles.title: Should ventilatory efficiency be considered when trading tidal volume against respiratory rate?
Derivation and Validation of Operational Definitions From Claims Data for Identifying Cardiogenic Shock.
articles.abstract: To derive and validate a claims-based operational definition for cardiogenic shock (CS) using administrative data against clinically adjudicated reference standards. Diagnostic accuracy study. Two independent clinical cohorts, a single-center cardiac ICU (CICU) registry and a multicenter CS registry (REtrospective and prospective observational Study to investigate Clinical oUtcomes and Efficacy of left ventricular assist device for Korean patients with cardiogenic shock [RESCUE]), and a nationwide administrative database from the Korean National Health Insurance Service. A total of 10,156 patients from the CICU registry and 1,247 patients from the RESCUE registry. For population-level application, 207,419 patients were identified from the national claims database. None. A claims-based algorithm defined CS using the International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision code R57.0 or cardiac disease codes combined with treatment-based criteria reflecting hemodynamic support, including mechanical circulatory support or vasoactive therapy. In the CICU cohort, the algorithm demonstrated a sensitivity of 0.89 and specificity of 0.90, with an overall accuracy of 0.90. In the RESCUE cohort, sensitivity was 0.95. When applied to the nationwide database, 207,419 patients with CS were identified. The cumulative mortality rates were 37.9% at 12 months, 49.9% at 5 years, and 61.7% at 10 years. A claims-based definition combining diagnostic codes with treatment-based criteria demonstrated high diagnostic performance for identifying CS. This approach enables reliable large-scale epidemiologic studies and long-term outcome assessments using administrative data and may facilitate system-level evaluation of critical care delivery in patients with CS.

articles.title: Apixaban vs rivaroxaban for venous thromboembolism: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Direct oral anticoagulants are first-line therapy for venous thromboembolism (VTE), yet comparative evidence between apixaban and rivaroxaban remains limited. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of apixaban versus rivaroxaban in patients with VTE. A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library was conducted from inception through March 2026. Studies directly comparing apixaban and rivaroxaban in adult VTE patients were included. Outcomes, including recurrent VTE, major bleeding, all-cause mortality, and net clinical harm, were pooled using a random-effects model. Thirteen studies comprising more than 220,000 patients were included. Apixaban was associated with a significantly lower risk of recurrent VTE compared to rivaroxaban (RR 0.85; 95% CI 0.74-0.98), with moderate heterogeneity. Apixaban was also associated with a significant 28% reduction in major bleeding risk (RR 0.72; 95% CI 0.65-0.81), with low heterogeneity, indicating consistent findings across studies. When efficacy and safety outcomes were combined, apixaban demonstrated a significantly lower risk of net clinical harm (RR 0.76; 95% CI 0.68-0.86). In contrast, no statistically significant difference was observed in all-cause mortality (RR 0.95; 95% CI 0.80-1.12), with substantial heterogeneity across studies. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of these findings, with no single study significantly altering the overall estimates. Overall, apixaban demonstrated a more favorable efficacy and safety profile compared with rivaroxaban in VTE management, with reduced recurrence and bleeding risk, while mortality remained comparable. These findings suggest that apixaban may be associated with a more favorable efficacy and safety profile than rivaroxaban; however, the results should be interpreted cautiously given the predominance of observational evidence.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of shock index, revised trauma score, and injury severity score for mortality prediction in trauma: A hierarchical meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Shock Index (SI) and Revised Trauma Score (RTS) are physiological tools available at the point of trauma triage. Injury Severity Score (ISS) is an anatomical score that requires completed injury characterization and is typically available only after initial resuscitation. Their comparative value for predicting mortality and whether ISS meaningfully adds to the acute tools remains unclear. The aim of this systematic review and hierarchical meta-analysis is to pool the diagnostic accuracy of SI and RTS as acute mortality-prediction tools in adult trauma patients; to benchmark these against ISS; and to formally test, in studies reporting both, whether RTS and ISS differ in diagnostic accuracy. Electronic databases were searched from inception to May 2026. In-hospital mortality was prespecified as the primary endpoint. Pooled sensitivity, specificity and hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) analyses were performed with a bivariate random-effects model for each tool separately. For studies reporting both RTS and ISS in the same cohort, a paired comparison was performed using a bivariate model with test type as a covariate and a pooled within-study difference analysis. Twelve studies (234,129 patients) were included. Pooled sensitivity/specificity were 0.679/0.763 for SI (5 studies, AUC 0.747), 0.788/0.801 for RTS (6 studies, AUC 0.852), and 0.788/0.796 for ISS (9 studies, AUC 0.855). In the six studies reporting both RTS and ISS, a paired bivariate comparison found no significant difference in diagnostic accuracy (likelihood-ratio test, p = 0.91; within-study sensitivity OR 1.59, 95% CI 0.82-3.07; specificity OR 0.89, 95% CI 0.55-1.45). RTS and ISS did not differ significantly in a formal paired comparison, and neither tool, alone, reliably rules in or out death at realistic trauma prevalence. SI, RTS and ISS should be understood as serving different, complementary roles across the trauma timeline - SI and RTS at the point of acute triage, ISS as a later anatomical benchmark - rather than as competing predictors to be ranked against one another.

articles.title: Association of loneliness and substance use among emergency department patients.
articles.journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
articles.abstract: Loneliness is associated with numerous adverse health outcomes. However, little is known about its relationship with substance use among emergency department (ED) patients, a population at elevated risk for substance use and related harms. We examined associations between loneliness and past 90-day substance use among ED patients. A convenience sample of patients aged 18-75 years was recruited from an urban academic ED between March 2025 and January 2026 (N = 300). Loneliness was assessed using the UCLA Loneliness Scale (UCLA-20; range = 20 to 80). The Tobacco, Alcohol, Prescription Medication, and Other Substance Use (TAPS) tool assessed binge alcohol use, cannabis use, and illicit drug use, including crack/cocaine, sedatives/hypnotics, opioids, and polydrug use. Multivariable logistic regression models examined associations between loneliness and substance use outcomes, adjusting for demographic characteristics, cigarette use and anxiety and depression symptoms. Each one-point increase in loneliness was associated with greater odds of illicit drug use (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 1.07, 95% confidence interval [CI]:1.03-1.11), including use of opioids (aOR = 1.10, 95% CI:1.03-1.19), crack/cocaine (aOR = 1.06, 95% CI:1.01-1.13), and polydrug use (aOR = 1.04, 95% CI:1.01-1.08). Loneliness was independently associated with recent illicit drug use. These findings suggest that loneliness may be an important and underrecognized correlate of high-risk substance use in ED populations. Incorporating loneliness assessment into ED screening workflows may help identify patients at elevated risk for substance-related harms and inform interventions aimed at improving engagement with substance use treatment and supportive services.

articles.title: Sputum cellularity and health services utilization among patients with asthma and COPD.
articles.abstract: Associations between health services utilization (HSU) and objectively measured airway inflammation in severe asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) patients remain unclear. Is there an association between quantitative sputum cell counts and HSU (hospitalizations, physician visits, emergency department visits) patterns in patients with asthma and COPD? In this retrospective cohort study, clinical data, spirometry, and sputum cell counts (% of eosinophils, neutrophils) obtained during routine clinical assessment of patients attending a university tertiary airway disease clinic were linked to Ontario health administrative databases (2006-2019). Sputum inflammatory cell counts were treated as fixed baseline exposure variables and negative binomial regression models using generalized estimating equations estimated RRs and 95% CIs for subsequent HSU adjusting for demographic, socioeconomic, and clinical covariates. Of the 4821 patients included, 3714(77%) had asthma only and 1107(23%) had COPD only. Among patients with asthma, sputum eosinophilia (>3%) was associated with higher asthma-specific HSU. Compared with patients with sputum eosinophils <3%, both the 3-15% and >15% eosinophil groups had similarly increased rates of asthma-specific emergency department visits (RR=1.92, 95%CI:1.49-2.47 and RR=1.88, 95%CI:1.17-3.03). Conversely, sputum eosinophil counts were not significantly associated with HSU in COPD, whereas high sputum neutrophil counts were associated with increased all-cause hospitalizations (RR=1.71, 95%CI:1.11-2.64). Overall, those with higher eosinophil (>15%) and lower neutrophil counts (<65%) had significantly higher rates of asthma-specific and asthma-related HSU. In contrast, sputum eosinophil counts were not significantly associated with increased all-cause hospitalizations among patients with COPD. Sputum eosinophilia (>3%) is associated with increased asthma-related HSU, whereas sputum eosinophils were not associated with increased HSU in COPD. These findings support the clinical relevance of airway inflammometry in asthma and highlight important differences in inflammatory phenotypes between asthma and COPD. Further studies are needed to better understand the mechanisms underlying these associations.

articles.title: CEUS- versus US- and CT-guided Biopsy for Subpleural Lung Lesions: A Prospective, Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: Ultrasound (US)-guided percutaneous lung needle biopsy (PLNB), the guideline-recommended approach for subpleural lung lesion (SLL) diagnosis, requires comparison with CT-guided biopsy based on high-level evidence clinical studies. Is US-guided PLNB superior to CT-guided biopsy in diagnostic performance and safety, and does CEUS provide further advantages? Participants undergoing PLNB for SLLs between June 2020 and November 2023 were randomized to US-, CEUS- and CT-guided biopsies. The dual primary outcomes were diagnostic yield and disease-specific diagnostic sensitivity. Diagnostic yield was defined according to the strict ATS/ACCP definition as the proportion of biopsies yielding clinically actionable diagnoses, while sensitivity referred to the proportion of patients with a confirmed disease correctly identified by biopsy. Four secondary outcomes included complication rate, CNB/FNA utilization, puncture number, and puncture time, with the overall complication rate adopted as the key safety indicator. A total of 2485 participants were randomized into the US (n=828), CEUS (n=829) and CT (n=828) groups. The CEUS-guided biopsy achieved the highest diagnostic yield (CEUS: 88.8%[736/829] vs. CT: 78.9%[653/828] vs. US: 76.0%[629/828], χ2=49.046, P <0.001) , as well as the highest diagnostic sensitivity (CEUS: 86.1%[714/829] vs. CT: 74.3%[615/828] vs. US: 68.7%[569/828], χ2=72.623, P <0.001). For disease-specific analysis, CEUS yielded superior diagnostic sensitivity for malignant subtypes (CEUS: 91.8%[563/613] vs. CT: 83.2%[520/625] vs. US: 75.2%[479/637], χ2=62.259, P <0.001) and specific benign disorders (CEUS: 69.9%[151/216] vs. CT: 46.8%[95/203] vs. US: 47.1%[90/191], χ2=29.712, P <0.001). Furthermore, the CEUS group exhibited the lowest overall complication rate (CEUS: 4.6%[38/828] vs. US: 7.5%[60/802] vs. CT: 15.8%[127/805], χ2=65.322, P <0.001). For SLL biopsy, CEUS-guided PLNB outperforms US- and CT-guided approaches in both diagnostic performance and procedural safety. CEUS guidance notably improves disease-specific diagnostic sensitivity for malignant subtypes and specific benign pulmonary disorders, serving as an optimal technique for clinical percutaneous lung biopsy. articles.title: TISA-818, an Anti-inflammatory Conjugate of Montelukast-Decapeptide, in Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome Due to Pulmonary Infection: A Phase 2 Randomized Trial Using the 2023 Global Definition.
articles.abstract: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) remains associated with substantial mortality. The 2023 global definition includes non-intubated patients, creating an opportunity to evaluate therapies earlier in the disease course. Is TISA-818 safe and potentially efficacious in patients with ARDS, particularly those who are non-intubated? This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter phase 2 trial was, to our knowledge, the first in China to use the 2023 global ARDS definition. Fifty-eight patients were randomized 1:1:1 to intravenous TISA-818 6 mg twice daily (BID), 12 mg once daily (QD), or matched placebo for 14 days. The primary endpoint was safety. Key secondary endpoints included respiratory support-free days (RSFDs) through day 28, proportion of patients alive and free from respiratory support at day 14, clinical improvement rate at day 14, and length of stay through 28 days. TISA-818 demonstrated an acceptable safety profile with comparable rates of treatment-emergent adverse events (AEs) and no unexpected safety signals. Treatment-related AEs were mild-to-moderate and occurred in 5.3%, 36.8%, and 21.1% of patients in the placebo, 6 mg BID, and 12 mg QD groups, respectively. Day-28 mortality was 5.3%, 10.5%, and 26.3%, whereas day-60 mortality was 26.3%, 21.1%, and 31.6% for placebo, 6 mg BID, and 12 mg QD, respectively. No drug-related serious AEs or deaths occurred. In the prespecified non-intubated subgroup (n=27, 9 per arm), exploratory analyses numerically favored 6 mg BID over placebo, with more RSFDs (difference, 6 days; 95% confidence interval, -3 to 15) and consistent numerical improvements across all secondary outcomes. TISA-818 was generally well tolerated. Day-28 mortality was numerically imbalanced but not sustained, likely reflecting small-sample variability; cautious interpretation is warranted. Consistent improvements across all efficacy endpoints, particularly with 6 mg BID in non-intubated patients, support further investigation in adequately powered trials.

articles.title: Correction: Evaluation of pre-endoscopy risk scores and base deficit for prediction adverse clinical outcomes in patients with upper gastrointestinal bleeding.
Diagnostic performance and timeliness of ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy for peripheral lymphadenopathy in Internal Medicine: a multicenter real-world study.
articles.abstract: Ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy (CNB) is increasingly used for evaluating peripheral lymphadenopathy, but evidence regarding its implementation in Internal Medicine remains limited. We assessed its diagnostic performance, safety, and diagnostic timeliness in routine clinical practice. This retrospective multicenter study included consecutive patients undergoing ultrasound-guided CNB of peripheral lymphadenopathy in five Internal Medicine departments between February 2021 and March 2026. The primary outcome was diagnostic performance. Secondary outcomes included safety, diagnostic timeliness, performance in lymphoma patients, and factors associated with obtaining a definitive diagnosis. A total of 413 patients were included (median age 62 years; 41.3% women). Lymphoma and carcinoma accounted for 44.1% and 23.7% of final diagnoses, respectively. The first CNB provided a definitive diagnosis in 85.7% of patients and a suggestive diagnosis in 8.0%, yielding an overall diagnostic yield of 93.7%. No major complications occurred. Median time from biopsy request to procedure was 1 day (IQR 0-2), and median time to definitive diagnosis was 10 days (IQR 6-16). Surgical biopsy was required in 9.4% of patients and was associated with longer diagnostic delays (42 vs 9 days; p < 0.001). Among 182 patients with lymphoma, overall diagnostic yield was 93.4%. Lower operator experience and hospital size < 500 beds were independently associated with a lower likelihood of obtaining a definitive diagnosis. Ultrasound-guided CNB of peripheral lymphadenopathy performed by internists demonstrated high diagnostic yield, excellent safety, and short diagnostic timelines in a large multicenter real-world cohort. Operator experience and institutional context may influence diagnostic performance.

articles.title: Renal trauma in a pediatric Level 1 trauma center: morbidity, mortality, and the role of renal scintigraphy.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Pediatric renal trauma is uncommon but potentially serious, and is often managed conservatively. Complications may occur, and the clinical value of renal scintigraphy during follow-up remains unclear. This study aimed to assess morbidity and mortality after pediatric renal trauma and to assess the clinical value of renal scintigraphy during follow-up. This retrospective single-center cohort study included pediatric trauma patients (< 18 years) with renal injuries admitted to a Level 1 trauma center in the Netherlands between January 1, 2001, and December 31, 2024. Mortality and in-hospital complications were assessed, and associations between renal scintigraphy abnormalities and complications during follow-up were evaluated. A total of 72 patients were included, of whom all injuries resulted from blunt trauma. Conservative management was applied in 88% of cases; embolization and nephrectomy were performed in 8% and 3% of patients, respectively. In-hospital mortality was 11% and was attributed exclusively to concomitant traumatic brain injury. Complications occurred in 25% of patients, primarily infections (19%), followed by hypertension during follow up (4%). Renal scintigraphy was performed in 53% of patients, predominantly in those with high-grade injuries; abnormalities were frequently observed (77%) but did not correlate with the occurrence of hypertension, proteinuria, or renal insufficiency during follow-up. Pediatric renal trauma, including high-grade injuries, can often be managed conservatively, and most complications can be treated using medical therapy or minimally invasive interventions. Renal scintigraphy showed no clear association with long-term morbidity and had limited additional value in routine follow-up. Given the potential for late-onset hypertension, structured long-term clinical surveillance with periodic monitoring of blood pressure, proteinuria, and renal function is warranted, particularly after high-grade injuries.

articles.title: Impella in infarction-related cardiogenic shock: evidence, complications, and implementation of microaxial LV unloading.
articles.abstract: Acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) remains highly lethal despite early revascularization. Although left ventricular (LV) failure predominates, AMI-CS may also be triggered or dominated by right ventricular (RV) failure, which carries distinct implications for the choice of mechanical support. Escalating catecholamines may increase afterload, provoke arrhythmias, and raise myocardial oxygen demand. Microaxial left ventricular (LV) support (Impella) provides forward flow while unloading the LV, potentially improving the subendocardial perfusion gradient, reducing pulmonary congestion, and limiting catecholamine exposure. Net clinical benefit is conditional and must be balanced against a substantial and predictable complication burden (major bleeding, vascular/limb complications, hemolysis with acute kidney injury, and infection). In the DanGer Shock trial, a protocolized Impella CP strategy in selected patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)-CS lowered 180-day mortality (45.8% vs. 58.5%; hazard ratio [HR]: 0.74) but increased major complications and renal replacement therapy. Conversely, early venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO [extracorporal membrane oxygenation]) in the ECLS (extra corporal life support)-SHOCK trial did not improve 30-day survival and increased bleeding and vascular complications. Clinically, Impella should be used as part of phenotype-driven shock pathways-early for LV-dominant, congested low-output shock with a reversible trajectory-combined with standardized access/anticoagulation bundles, close complication surveillance, and early reassessment with deliberate escalation or de-escalation.

articles.title: Prehospital severity and in-hospital mortality in trauma patients managed by the Friuli-Venezia Giulia helicopter emergency medical service: a 6-year retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Data on in-hospital mortality among trauma patients managed by Helicopter Emergency Medical Services (HEMS) in Italy remain limited. We aimed to describe the epidemiology and in-hospital mortality of trauma patients transported after management by the Friuli-Venezia Giulia HEMS and to assess prehospital factors associated with death. We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study including trauma patients managed by HEMS FVG and transported to hospital, either directly by HEMS or after continuation of transport by ground emergency medical services, between 2018 and 2023. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Jeffreys-prior penalized logistic regression was used to reduce sparse-data bias and instability from separation. The RTS-based model was designated as the primary model and the NACA-based model as a secondary sensitivity analysis. Model performance was assessed internally, and the functional forms of both age and RTS were examined using restricted cubic splines. Of 3,357 trauma records in the source cohort, 205 prehospital deaths were excluded from the in-hospital mortality analysis, leaving 3,152 transported patients. Outcome data were available for 3,143 patients, of whom 107 died in hospital (3.4%). In the primary RTS-based model, older age, lower RTS, tracheal intubation, and prehospital CPR were associated with mortality. Compared with RTS ≥ 7, adjusted ORs were 2.36 (95% CI 1.11-5.50) for RTS 4-<7 and 5.19 (95% CI 1.64-17.04) for RTS < 4. Age was associated with mortality (OR 1.03 per year, 95% CI 1.01-1.04). Continuous RTS analysis was concordant (OR 0.68 per one-point increase, 95% CI 0.54-0.86; p = 0.0013). Among trauma patients transported to hospital after HEMS management, older age, higher prehospital injury severity, tracheal intubation, and prehospital CPR were associated with in-hospital mortality. Intubation and CPR should be interpreted primarily as markers of severe physiological compromise rather than causal determinants of death.

articles.title: Flood Response in Rural Indonesia Implementing the World Health Organization Emergency Medical Team Minimum Data Set - Disaster Report.
articles.abstract: Indonesia experiences recurrent natural disasters that impose substantial strain on its health system, with annual flooding affecting rural communities such as Sitiarjo Sumbermanjing Wetan. Despite these recurring events, Indonesia has not systematically adopted the World Health Organization (WHO) Emergency Medical Team (EMT) Minimum Data Set (MDS) for standardized disaster medical reporting, thereby limiting data integration and evidence-based policy development. This disaster report describes the operational patterns, clinical demographics, and syndromic distribution captured by the WHO EMT MDS framework across three distinct flood responses in 2017, 2022, and 2023. The Universitas Brawijaya Emergency Medical Team (UB-EMT) prospectively collected daily surveillance data using the WHO EMT MDS reporting system. A total of 363 consultations were analyzed and stratified according to age, sex, and reporting period. Consultation volume peaked on Day 1 and declined on subsequent days. Females accounted for 62% of the cases and adults (18-64 years old) represented the majority of patients (68.87%). The most frequently reported conditions were skin diseases (33.46%), musculoskeletal problems (24.39%), and acute respiratory infections (16.64%), respectively. Age-specific patterns were evident: preschoolers and school-aged children presented with acute respiratory infections, whereas adults and older people more commonly experienced skin diseases and musculoskeletal problems. The absence of systematic implementation of the WHO EMT MDS constrains standardized surveillance and inter-team coordination in disaster settings. Therefore, the institutional adoption of the WHO EMT MDS is essential to strengthen real-time monitoring, optimize resource allocation, and enhance post-disaster evaluation in Indonesia.

articles.title: Impact of antithrombotic therapy on management and prognosis of patients hospitalized for upper gastrointestinal bleeding: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Antithrombotic agents are frequently implicated in upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB), yet their impact on prognosis and management remains unclear. The aim of this study was to assess the impact of pre-existing antithrombotic therapy on the management and prognosis of patients hospitalized for UGIB. This study used data from a retrospective, multicenter cohort of adult patients hospitalized for UGIB between January 2019 and December 2020 in Greater Paris University Hospitals. Patients were categorized into four groups according to their pre-existing antithrombotic treatment: antiplatelet therapy, anticoagulant therapy, both, or none. The primary outcome was thirty-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included endoscopy, endoscopic hemostasis, and blood transfusion within 7 days, and intensive care unit admission. Associations were assessed using multivariable logistic regression and reported as adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (95%CIs). Among 928 patients, 226 (24%) were on antiplatelet therapy alone, 154 (17%) on anticoagulant therapy alone, 61 (7%) on combined therapy, and 487 (52%) received no antithrombotic treatment. Thirty-day mortality was 6.9%: 8.4% in the no-antithrombotic group, 6.2% in the antiplatelet group, 4.5% in the anticoagulant group, and 3.3% in the combined therapy group. Compared with the no-antithrombotic group, anticoagulant therapy alone was associated with lower mortality (aOR=0.28, 95% CI 0.10-0.83), while antiplatelet therapy alone or combined therapy were not significantly associated (aOR=0.47, 95% CI 0.19-1.14 and aOR=0.12, 95% CI 0.01-1.11, respectively). Neither anticoagulant nor antiplatelet therapy was associated with secondary outcomes. Antithrombotic therapy had no negative impact on the management or prognosis of patients hospitalized for UGIB.

articles.title: A Robust Educational Initiative for EMS Clinicians Focusing on Pit-Crew CPR Improves Neurologically Intact Survival.
articles.abstract: To evaluate whether the implementation of a region-wide pit-crew cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) initiative was associated with improved survival to hospital discharge with good neurological function among adults with non-traumatic out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) in a heterogenous, multi-agency emergency medical services (EMS) system in south-central Connecticut. We conducted a retrospective, before-and-after observational study using the Cardiac Arrest Registry to Enhance Survival (CARES). The pit-crew CPR intervention, comprising structured didactic and hands-on simulation-based training was delivered across 27 EMS agencies from September 28, 2021 through August 2, 2022. The primary outcome was survival to hospital discharge with good neurological function (Cerebral Performance Category 1-2). Secondary outcomes included survival to hospital discharge and sustained return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC). We performed an interrupted time series analysis using the beginning of our intervention (September 28, 2021) as the interruption to model. Multivariable logistic regression models were adjusted for age, sex, race, shockable initial rhythm, witnessed arrest, arrest location, and bystander CPR. A total of 1917 adult non-traumatic OHCA patients (922 pre-intervention; 995 post-intervention) were resuscitated by EMS clinicians in the study period. In progression since intervention, there was a significant increase in neurologically intact survival per 4-month interval (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 1.20; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.01-1.44), suggesting a gradual improvement in outcomes over time after protocol implementation. At intervention start, there was a significant increase in ROSC (aOR 1.41; 95% CI, 1.1-1.81). There was no change in survival to hospital discharge prior to the intervention, at the time of the intervention, or following the intervention. Implementation of a pit-crew CPR model across a heterogenous, multi-agency EMS system was associated with a significant gradual increase in neurologically intact survival in the post-intervention period, as well as a significant immediate improvement in ROSC at the time of protocol implementation. These findings support structured, team-based resuscitation as a feasible and effective strategy to improve cardiac arrest outcomes within existing EMS systems.

articles.title: The Future of Cardiac Care: A Review on the Role for Non-Invasive, Home-Based Monitoring and Rehabilitation after Hospitalisation for Acute Decompensated Heart Failure.
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is characterised by recurrent decompensation leading to worsening of symptoms and unplanned hospitalisations. Patients often experience poor post-hospitalisation recovery, fail to maintain functional capacity, and demonstrate a high risk for re-admission. In this review we discuss these challenges, and explore how non-invasive, digital solutions may improve health outcomes. In contrast to current episodic surveillance, advances in wearable sensor technologies enable continuous, non-invasive monitoring to facilitate physiology-guided management to improve early clinical stabilisation. Additionally, trials have highlighted the potential of exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation to improve functional capacity in HF patients. Finally, continuous monitoring of relevant physiological signals, through developing algorithms, have the potential for early prediction of clinical deterioration. Non-invasive, co-created digital solutions may facilitate early stabilisation, improve functional capacity and predict clinical deterioration following episodes of decompensation. Collectively, they may enhance clinical outcomes and quality of life in patients with HF.

articles.title: Epidemiological patterns and surgical outcomes of pediatric supracondylar humerus fractures: a focus on domestic safety and seasonal variations.
articles.abstract: Supracondylar humerus fractures (SHFs) are prevalent pediatric elbow injuries. This study investigates the epidemiology, clinical characteristics, and treatment outcomes of pediatric SHFs to identify preventive strategies. This retrospective study included 298 pediatric patients (aged ≤14 years) treated for SHFs between December 2018 and June 2024. Demographic data, injury mechanisms, seasonal variations, and surgical details were analyzed. Radiological reduction was assessed via the Baumann angle and anterior humeral line. Functional outcomes were evaluated using Flynn's criteria. The study cohort (mean age 6.1 years; 58.7% male) predominantly sustained extension-type fractures (96.3%), with the severely displaced Gartland Type III being the most frequent (49.3%). The incidence of injuries peaked during the summer months and school holidays, with the majority occurring at home (64.1%) due to simple falls (93%). Surgical intervention, consisting of closed reduction and percutaneous pinning, was necessitated in 75.8% of cases, with a mean time-to-surgery of 4.6 h. Satisfactory (excellent and good) functional outcomes were achieved in 97.9% of the patients. Overall complication rates were minimal, and transient nerve injuries (2%) fully resolved spontaneously during follow-up. Pediatric SHFs frequently occur in domestic settings during the summer months, strongly highlighting the need for "safe home" modifications and parental education. Despite a high prevalence of severely displaced fractures, prompt surgical intervention and meticulous anatomical reduction yield excellent long-term functional outcomes and minimize complications.

articles.title: Life-course hygiene exposures and disorders of gut-brain interaction: a multinational cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Despite growing interest in its role in immune-mediated diseases, the relevance of the hygiene hypothesis to disorders of gut-brain interaction (DGBI) remains unclear. We aimed to examine the associations between childhood and adulthood hygiene-related exposures and DGBI prevalence, and to assess whether these associations persist after adjustment for sociodemographic and national development indicators. This cross-sectional study included 54,127 adults from 26 countries. DGBI were defined using Rome IV criteria. Childhood (≤ 7 years) and adulthood hygiene-related exposures included farm residence and access to running water, electricity, and rural residence. Country-level development was assessed using the Human Development Index (HDI). After adjustment for sociodemographic factors and psychological distress, several individual exposures showed independent associations with DGBI. Childhood farm exposure was independently associated with higher odds of DGBI (OR=1.11, 95% CI 1.03-1.19), irritable bowel syndrome (OR=1.21, 95% CI 1.03-1.42), and functional dyspepsia (OR=1.22, 95% CI 1.08-1.38). In contrast, rural residence (OR=0.88, 95% CI 0.82-0.95) and absence of running water (OR=0.83, 95% CI 0.77-0.90) or electricity (OR=0.86, 95% CI 0.77-0.97) in adulthood were associated with lower odds of DGBI. These associations remained statistically significant after additional adjustment for HDI. Several individual hygiene-related environmental exposures were associated with DGBI, suggesting that environmental conditions may be associated with global variation in DGBI burden.

articles.title: Respiratory function, functional capacity, dyspnea, and sleep quality in young adults using the IQOS heated tobacco product: a matched cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: This matched cross-sectional study compared respiratory function, respiratory muscle strength, functional exercise capacity, dyspnea, and sleep quality between young IQOS users and matched control subjects. This study involved 31 young adult IQOS users and 31 age/sex/body mass index-matched never-tobacco users who underwent a standardized testing protocol during a single visit. Spirometry, maximal inspiratory pressure (MIP), 6-min walk test (6MWT), modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) dyspnea scale, modified Borg Scale (mBorg), and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) scores were compared. While mean resting lung functions were similar between groups (all p > 0.05), IQOS users had shorter 6MWT distances (591.1 [580.2 - 638.4] meters vs. 626.0 [600.5 - 683.8] meters, p = 0.003, r = 0.53) and higher mMRC dyspnea scores (median mMRC Grade = 1 (0-1) in IQOS users vs 0 (0-0) in controls, p < 0.001, r = 0.62), higher mBorg dyspnea scores at the end of the 6MWT (median end-6MWT mBorg rating scale 1 [0-2] vs 0 [0-1], p = 0.001, r = 0.57), and poor sleep quality (PSQI global score 6.32 ± 2.63 vs 4.58 ± 1.61, p = 0.012, r = 0.45). Additionally, while MIP values tended toward being lower in IQOS users, these differences were statistically nonsignificant (p = 0.090). In conclusion, young exclusive IQOS users showed lower functional exercise capacity, greater dyspnea, and poorer sleep quality than matched never-users despite comparable resting spirometry, and these hypothesis-generating findings warrant longitudinal evaluation with biochemical exposure verification.

articles.title: Assessing health advocacy competencies through a novel simulation OSCE-based educational framework.
articles.abstract: Health advocacy remains one of the least explicitly assessed CanMEDS roles in Emergency Medicine. Objective structured clinical examination (OSCE) simulation is used to assess performance in real time but has not previously incorporated social determinants of health. We developed and piloted a simulation-based OSCE, embedding advocacy within acute clinical care and introduced novel assessment tools, completed by both examiners and standardized patients. Here we report the feasibility and acceptability of this OSCE and assessment tools. Twenty-two residents completed the advocacy and standard cases; 18 (82%) completed exit surveys. Most participants did not know advocacy would be assessed. Participants described the case as realistic and acceptable with minor suggestions for refinement. Assessors found the assessments intuitive to use and feasible to implement. This pilot suggests structured assessment of patient-level advocacy from both physician and patient perspectives can be feasibly integrated into simulation assessment without disrupting usual performance evaluation.

articles.title: Performance of updated American College of Surgeons field triage guidelines in identifying need for trauma center care.
articles.abstract: The Guidelines for the Field Triage of injured patients were updated in 2021 to improve the reliability of prehospital trauma triage. The objective of this study was to describe the association of the 2021 Field Triage Guidelines criteria with need for advanced trauma center care from a cohort of patients transported to a level 1 trauma center. This was a health records review of Field Triage Guidelines criteria met for trauma team activations at a level 1 trauma center from January 2020 to December 2021. Hospital-based and injury severity score (ISS)-based trauma center need were defined and sensitivity and specificity of the Field Triage Guidelines calculated for both. Area under the receiver operator curves were used to assess accuracy. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the association of each criterion with trauma center need. A total of 1427 patients were included and 90.3% met at least one Field Triage Guidelines criteria. Overall, patients meeting hospital-based trauma center need was 33.8% compared to 28.4% which met ISS-based trauma center need. Field Triage Guidelines criteria demonstrated a sensitivity of 97.3% and specificity of 13.3% with respect to hospital-based trauma center need with an area under the ROC of 0.80. Mental status and vital signs showed the highest association with trauma center need. The updated 2021 Field Triage Guidelines demonstrate good accuracy when assessed retrospectively on a cohort of patients transferred to a level 1 trauma center. The very high sensitivity of the new guidelines may help to reduce undertriage rates to the international goal of <5%. New criteria in this iteration of the Field Triage Guidelines could lead to improved rates of undertriage specifically in severely injured geriatric patients.

Surgeon-perceived intraoperative complexity is associated with early adverse outcomes after major emergency abdominal surgery: a prospective cohort study.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Intraoperative complexity in major emergency abdominal surgery lacks a standardized definition and is rarely quantified prospectively. Whether surgeon-perceived intraoperative complexity is associated with short-term postoperative outcomes remains unknown. In this single-center prospective cohort study, 411 patients undergoing major emergency abdominal surgery were included. Immediately after surgery, the operating surgeon rated perceived intraoperative complexity on a 0-10 scale. The association between surgeon-perceived intraoperative complexity and the primary outcome, 30-day unplanned reoperation, was investigated using Fine-Gray regression. The model was adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, performance status, and intraoperative pathology. Secondary outcomes were 30-day mortality, length of stay, and Comprehensive Complication Index. Unplanned reoperation occurred in 15% and 30-day mortality in 11%. Higher surgeon-perceived intraoperative complexity was associated with reoperation (sHR 1.20 per point; 95% CI 1.08-1.34). Complexity was also associated with prolonged LOS (β 1.47 days per unit increase; 95% CI 0.93-2.01), higher CCI category (OR 1.24 per unit increase; 95% CI 1.14-1.35), and increased 30-day mortality (OR 1.25; 95% CI 1.07-1.45). Surgeon-perceived intraoperative complexity was associated with reoperation, morbidity, and 30-day mortality after major emergency abdominal surgery. These findings suggest that the operating surgeon's assessment may capture clinically meaningful prognostic information beyond conventional baseline risk factors. External validation and evaluation of inter-rater reproducibility are needed before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Feasibility of Collaborative Assessment and Management of Suicidality-Brief Intervention in an Emergency Department With Youth Who Are Suicidal.
articles.abstract: Emergency departments (EDs) are key entry points for many youth experiencing suicidal thoughts and behaviors into mental health care. ED clinicians play a critical role in crisis intervention, prevention, and linking patients to ongoing care, yet many report uncertainty when assessing for and managing suicidal risk. The Collaborative Assessment and Management of suicidal thoughts and behaviors [Collaborative Assessment and Management of Suicidality (CAMS)] is an evidence-based, suicide-focused intervention that has been adapted into a single session [CAMS-Brief Intervention (CAMS-BI)]. This study tested the use of CAMS-BI with youth who are suicidal and presenting to a pediatric ED. Participants (aged 12 to 21 y; n = 20) were approached in the ED and completed distress measures before and after CAMS-BI. Following standard discharge timelines was prioritized. Analyses supported CAMS-BI's feasibility for ED youth populations, given the observed low rate of intervention refusal (8.7%) and high completion rate (87%). Participation in the study did not delay ED discharge times. Youth receiving CAMS-BI reported significantly lower distress postintervention, d = 0.45. Three-month follow-up indicated reductions in ED-return rates (0%) compared with youth who did not receive the intervention (15%), and strong patient engagement with outpatient treatment following CAMS-BI was notable (88% attended follow-up appointment). This pilot study provides evidence for CAMS-BI's feasibility for youth in fast-paced ED settings and its clinical value to quickly decrease distress. Future directions include larger, more rigorous replications to fine-tune CAMS-BI implementation into ED workflows.

articles.title: Autonomy in Fellowship Training and Its Influence on Self-Reported Self-Efficacy in Pediatric Emergency Medicine.
articles.abstract: This study examined the relationship between autonomy during pediatric emergency medicine (PEM) fellowship and self-efficacy in 6 Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education-defined entrustable professional activities (EPAs). We hypothesized that experiencing greater autonomy during fellowship would correlate with higher self-efficacy among current fellows and recent graduates. An anonymous electronic survey was distributed to current (2021-2022) second- and third-year PEM fellows and first- and second-year PEM attendings who graduated in 2020 and 2021. The survey collected demographic data, self-reported levels of autonomy during fellowship, and self-efficacy ratings for each EPA on a 0 to 100 scale, assessed both currently and retrospectively for 1 year prior. Autonomy was defined as ≥33% of clinical time in indirect supervision or independent practice. Statistical analyses included paired t tests, independent t tests, and multivariate analysis of covariance. One hundred twelve current fellows and 86 recent graduates responded (39% response rate). Both cohorts reported significant self-efficacy improvements across all 6 EPAs over the assessed period (P<0.001 for all comparisons). No significant differences in self-efficacy gains were observed between those who reported experiencing autonomy during fellowship and those who did not (P>0.05). In multivariate analysis, prior self-efficacy was the only consistent predictor of current self-efficacy (P<0.0001), explaining 53% to 71% of variance. This study found no association between self-reported autonomy in PEM fellowship training and self-efficacy in PEM-specific EPAs. Self-efficacy increased over time among all respondents regardless of autonomy experience. These findings suggest that the relationship between autonomy and trainee development may be more complex than previously assumed and warrants further investigation with refined measurement tools.

articles.title: Nitrous Oxide Use in Autistic Children: A Descriptive Study.
articles.abstract: Describe the population of autistic children who undergo nitrous oxide sedation and the rate of associated adverse events (AEs). Analyze patient- and procedure-level factors associated with AEs in autistic children receiving nitrous oxide outside the dental setting. A retrospective, descriptive study of autistic children, 3 to 18 years, who received nitrous oxide for procedural sedation during an emergency department or sedation encounter within a single hospital system between January 2014 and December 2023. Data extracted included patient demographics and comorbidities, as well as indication, maximum concentration, duration of administration, and AEs of nitrous oxide. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize the data. Analysis was performed on 186 patients [median age: 8 years (interquartile range: 5.2-12.75), 74.2% male]. Intravenous line placement was the most common indication in all locations. Most received 70% nitrous oxide with a median duration of 6 minutes (interquartile range: 4 -9.75). AEs were rare, occurring in only 3 patients (1.6%), with zero vomiting or aborted procedures. Given the rarity of AEs, no associated factors were able to be identified. Nitrous oxide is a safe, effective, and well-tolerated option for procedural sedation in autistic children, with a low rate of AEs. These findings add to the limited literature supporting its use in nondental settings and suggest it may be a valuable tool for facilitating minor procedures in this population. Future prospective studies are needed to optimize nitrous oxide delivery and determine factors contributing to AEs.

articles.title: Food Insecurity Screening and Immediate Access to Prepackaged Groceries in the Pediatric Emergency Department: A Pilot Study.
articles.abstract: Food insecurity (FI) is prevalent in many urban settings across the United States. Many vulnerable families who lack access to a medical home utilize the pediatric emergency department (PED), making the PED a critical access point to address FI. We aimed to understand caregivers' experiences in receiving prepackaged groceries and community resources within a PED. In this pilot initiative, caregivers who screened positive for FI in the PED received prepackaged groceries for their household and a list of community resources. Caregivers were interviewed to understand their experience in receiving food resources in the PED. Phone interviews were conducted until code saturation was reached. Interviews were recorded, transcribed, and coded. Content analysis generated themes describing the impact of the intervention. This study was conducted in a tertiary care PED in an urban setting between October 2018 and June 2019. Participants included English-speaking caregivers of children younger than 18 years. Ninety-six households received groceries and a list of community food resources. Four themes emerged from interviewing 23 caregivers: (1) immediate food relief was helpful when their child was acutely ill, (2) caregivers generally accepted the food from the prepackaged bags, (3) community resources were difficult to access, and (4) FI households who did not use community resources ascribed this to a lack of need for urgent food. Families perceived benefits of being provided groceries during emergency department visits since there are barriers to accessing community resources.

articles.title: Repeat 9-1-1 Calls and Clinical Outcomes of Children After Non-transport by Emergency Medical Services.
articles.abstract: Pediatric non-transport by emergency medical services (EMS) is common but there are limited data assessing patient outcomes. Our primary objective was to determine the proportion of children not transported by EMS who have a repeat 9-1-1 call and transport within 72 h. Our secondary objective was to determine whether patient demographic or clinical characteristics are associated with repeat 9-1-1 call and transport. We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study using the 2018-2022 ESO Data Collaborative research dataset. Of these records, one third are linked to hospital data which allowed for inclusion of discharge and ICD-10 diagnosis codes for some of the cases. We used descriptive statistics to compare cases (non-transported children aged 0-17 years with repeat 9-1-1 call and transport within 72 h) to controls (no repeat 9-1-1 call or repeat 9-1-1 call with non-transport). We conducted a multivariable logistic regression analysis to evaluate factors associated with a repeat 9-1-1 call and transport within 72 h. We generated descriptive statistics summarizing emergency department (ED) dispositions for the subset of patients where this data was available. Of 1,849,925 pediatric 9-1-1 calls, 732,525 (40%) were not transported by EMS. Within 72 h, 7,544 (1%) had repeat 9-1-1 call with transport to the ED. Repeat 9-1-1 call was associated with young age (0-4 years), Black, non-Hispanic race, male sex, calls from areas with a very low Child Opportunity Index (Opportunity Index), calls during out-of-office hours, and neurologic primary impressions. There were 11 (0.1%) deaths on scene upon repeat 9-1-1 call within 72 h of initial non-transport. Of the 1,001 (13%) patients with hospital-linked data, 814 (89%) were discharged from the ED, 162 (16%) were hospitalized, and two (0.2%) died. Only 1% of children not transported by EMS had a repeat 9-1-1 call and transport within 72 h. Hospitalization and death after non-transport were rare. These results may inform the development of safe and efficient pediatric non-transport protocols.

articles.title: Practice Patterns and Performance of Pediatric Air Medical Tracheal Intubation: A National Multisite Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Pediatric prehospital advanced airway management is high-stakes and low-frequency. Prior analyses have been limited to single-agency air medical groups or ground emergency medical services cohorts. National air medical performance is not well described. The aim of this study is to characterize practice patterns and outcomes of pediatric air medical intubation across a national multisite cohort. This was a retrospective cohort study of pediatric (<18 years) intubation encounters performed by air medical crews and recorded in ImageTrend Collaborate, a multisite prehospital clinical data repository, from 2021 to 2025. First-pass success, overall intubation success, and post-attempt physiology defined as a composite of hypoxia, age-adjusted hypotension, and age-adjusted bradycardia within 10 min after index attempt were summarized as n(%) or median (interquartile range [IQR]) and compared across four age groups (<1, 1-5, 6-10, 11-17 years) using chi-square or Fisher's exact tests. Site-level medication use was summarized among sites contributing 10 or more encounters. Among 1,040 encounters from 39 contributing sites across four United States regions, median age was 13 years (IQR 5-16) and 57.7% involved trauma or burn. A sedative-plus-paralytic strategy was used in 77.8% (809/1,040) with ketamine the most common induction agent (43.5% ketamine-only, 31.9% etomidate-only). Video laryngoscopy was documented in 8.6% of intubations. First-pass success was 86.5% (898/1,038) and overall success was 93.3% (968/1,038). Performance varied significantly by age with first-pass success at 69.1% (47/68) in infants under 1 year versus 88.7% (535/603) in adolescents (p < 0.001), overall success 80.9% (55/68) versus 93.9% (566/603), respectively (p < 0.001), and post-attempt physiologic instability 53.6% (30/56) versus 31.3% (175/560) respectively (p = 0.008). Post-attempt end-tidal carbon dioxide (ETCO2) within 10 min was documented in 82.8% (861/1,040) overall, and 60.0% (42/70) in infants (p < 0.001). Among the 13 sites with 10 or more encounters, peri-attempt ketamine share ranged from 9% to 84% and succinylcholine share from 0% to 91%. In this national multisite air medical cohort, overall airway performance was favorable, but infants younger than 1 year had lower first-pass success, lower overall intubation success, and less frequent post-intubation ETCO2 documentation. Substantial practice variation across contributing sites suggests opportunity for both targeted training in the infant subgroup and benchmarking across sites.

articles.title: Prevalence and psychosocial factors of PTSD among disaster-affected populations in India: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) is a widespread condition affecting individuals globally in the aftermath of disasters. For this review, the disaster-affected population refers to individuals or populations who have experienced a potentially traumatic event with psychosocial consequences. The current review aims to assess the prevalence and psychosocial factors of PTSD among disaster-affected populations in India. A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted in the present study. Relevant keywords were identified and used to search databases, including Scopus, PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Cochrane, as well as websites and reference lists, to identify eligible studies. The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) flow chart was used for the final included studies to reveal the results. The current review conducted a critical appraisal of the included studies by using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) quality evaluation. Meta-analysis using Jeffreys's Amazing Statistics Program (JASP) software and manual analysis was done to assess the psychosocial factors and conceptual framework. A total of 1370 documents were identified from the databases, and 151 documents were duplicates. Following title/abstract screening, 1178 studies were excluded, 21 full text not retrieved, and 20 studies were included for the final results. The critical appraisal results found that more than half of the studies demonstrated good methodological quality. The results revealed that the pooled prevalence of PTSD was 38%, with young populations disproportionately affected, although no significant associations were found with age group, disaster type, or region. Nineteen psychosocial risk factors were identified, prominently including loss of family members or pets and property damage. The conceptual framework highlights the interplay between traumatic events and psychosocial factors in PTSD outcomes. The findings underscore the need for multidisciplinary collaboration among mental health professionals, long-term intervention strategies, and evidence-based practices to address India's mental health challenges.

articles.title: Exercise, Nutrition and GLP-1 Medicines to Improve Body Weight and Muscle Function in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction.
articles.abstract: This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on lifestyle, pharmacological, surgical, and multimodal interventions targeting muscle strength, body composition, and functional capacity in HFpEF with sarcopenia and/or obesity. Exercise, particularly concurrent endurance and resistance training protocols, improve aerobic capacity, functional performance, symptoms, and quality of life in HFpEF. Protein supplementation may preserve muscle mass, while caloric restriction may enhance aerobic capacity and function butdecreases muscle mass. SGLT2i and GLP-1 medicines may reduce hospitalizations and improve symptoms, with GLP-1 medicines producing greater weight loss and performance benefits. Bariatric surgery may also achieve substantial weight loss and functional improvements, although evidence in HFpEF with obesity is limited. Obesity-related HFpEF may benefit from a combination of resistance exercise and adequate protein intake to preserve muscle during weight loss, while pharmacotherapy can be used to support cardiac function. Future trials should evaluate multimodal interventions to mitigate frailty risk in HFpEF.

articles.title: Injury patterns in a war zone: A comparative analysis of civilians and military personnel.
articles.abstract: Modern armed conflicts increasingly affect both civilians and defense forces, resulting in heterogeneous injury patterns driven by diverse mechanisms. Direct comparative data between these populations treated within the same healthcare system remain limited. To compare injury mechanisms, anatomical injury patterns, injury severity, and early clinical outcomes between civilians and defense forces casualties treated at a single tertiary trauma center during an active conflict. A retrospective analysis was conducted of all consecutive war-related trauma admissions between October 7, 2023, and January 7, 2024. Demographic data, injury mechanisms, anatomical sites, Injury Severity Score (ISS), emergency interventions, and early outcomes were collected. Percentage-based comparative plots were used to visualize injury mechanism and anatomical site distributions. The cohort included 192 patients (128 defense forces, 64 civilians). Civilians were older and included more females. Overall injury severity and rates of airway management, ventilatory support, and ICU admission were comparable between groups. Defense forces more frequently required direct transfer from the emergency department to the operating room (28% vs. 14%, p = 0.047). Shrapnel-related injuries were significantly more common among defense forces, whereas acoustic trauma was observed exclusively among civilians (36%, p < 0.001). Injury-mechanism profiles differed between groups, whereas no statistically significant differences were observed in the proportions of patients injured at the individual anatomical site. Despite similar overall injury severity, civilians and defense forces exhibit distinct injury profiles. Civilians are disproportionately affected by acoustic trauma, highlighting population-specific vulnerabilities with implications for triage, diagnostic evaluation, and trauma system preparedness, especially during mass casualty incidents, when rapid recognition of group-specific injury patterns is essential for appropriate resource prioritization and allocation.

articles.title: Force measurement in circular external fixation frames reflects construct stability: A laboratory proof-of-concept study.
articles.abstract: Circular external fixation frames are widely used in limb reconstruction, however determining the optimal time for frame removal remains challenging. Current approaches rely on clinical and radiological assessment, both of which have recognised limitations. Mechanical assessment of construct stability offers a potential alternative, but existing approaches have not translated widely into clinical practice, in part due to reliance on absolute measurement thresholds. To determine whether force measurement within a circular external fixation frame varies systematically with fracture site stability, and to assess whether this measurement may support monitoring of healing progression. Three similar four-ring Ilizarov frame constructs were assembled using a Perspex bone analogue. A load cell was integrated into the frame and used to measure force during axial loading to 700 N. Models representing different stages of fracture healing were simulated using varying fracture gaps and materials of differing stiffness. Measurements were obtained across multiple sensor positions and configurations. Force measurements were compared between models using non-parametric statistical methods. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to assess separation between conditions. Force measured within the frame decreased progressively with increasing construct stiffness. A significant relationship between model stability and measured force was observed (Kruskal-Wallis p < 0.0001). Clear separation was demonstrated between grossly unstable and intact constructs; however, overlap between higher stability models and intact bone was evident. ROC analysis showed strong discrimination when considering all unstable conditions (AUC ≥ 0.91), but performance was reduced when restricted to higher stability models (AUC 0.699-0.838). Absolute force measurements varied with sensor configuration, although the rank order of conditions was preserved. Force measurement within a circular external fixation frame reflects construct stability in an in vitro model. Whilst absolute values are dependent on construct configuration and show reduced discrimination near union, consistent directional changes suggest that serial within-subject measurement may provide a useful approach to monitoring healing progression. These findings support further evaluation of longitudinal measurement strategies in clinical studies.

articles.title: Screening for posttraumatic stress symptoms after accidental injury: Implementation of the young child PTSD screen in the acute trauma setting.
articles.abstract: Post-traumatic stress symptoms (PTSS) in young children are underrecognized following unintentional injury, and validated screening tools for early childhood are rarely implemented in acute trauma settings. We evaluated the Young Child PTSD Screen (YCPS) administered at hospital discharge to determine screening positivity, associated clinical factors, and persistence of symptoms at one month. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of children aged 2-6 years admitted to a Level I pediatric trauma center following unintentional injury (November 2020-November 2024). Caregivers completed the 6-item YCPS at discharge. Children with ≥ 1 endorsed symptom were contacted one month later for repeat assessment. Demographic, injury, and hospitalization data were abstracted from the trauma registry and electronic health record. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated predictors of positive screening at discharge, and follow-up analyses assessed persistence of symptoms. Of 193 screened patients, 186 met inclusion criteria. Over half (55.9%, n = 104) screened symptomatic or positive at discharge. On univariate analysis, greater injury severity score and longer length of stay were associated with symptomatic/positive screening. In multivariable analysis, injury severity remained the only significant predictor (aOR 1.07 per point increase in injury severity score, 95% CI 1.02-1.13, p = 0.004). Of eligible children, 32.6% (n = 34) completed one-month follow-up and 41.1% (n = 14) screened positive. Higher discharge YCPS scores were associated with positive follow-up (median 3 vs 2; p = 0.046) and were positively correlated with one-month scores (r²=0.21, p = 0.005). No demographic variables (age, sex, race) predicted persistence of symptoms. Over one-third of traumatically injured young children screened positive for PTSS at discharge, and a substantial proportion had persistent symptoms at one month. Injury severity was associated with positive screens at discharge, while early symptom burden predicted persistence. These findings support the feasibility and clinical value of implementing developmentally sensitive screening for very young children in the inpatient trauma setting.

articles.title: Patterns of multimorbidity and in-hospital kidney function decline in older adults: a latent class analysis of three acute-care cohorts.
articles.abstract: Multimorbidity is associated with an increased risk of renal function decline in older individuals. In this study, we aimed to evaluate whether multimorbidity patterns differently contributed to this risk in three different hospital settings. We conducted a comparative cohort study of patients aged ≥ 65 years admitted to acute-care hospitals in Italy. Data were drawn from the retrospective SIN-SIGG study (geriatric units, n = 1600; nephrology units, n = 560) and the prospective REPOSI registry (internal medicine units, n = 4595). Quantitative multimorbidity was defined as the number of chronic conditions with prevalence ≥ 5% per cohort; qualitative multimorbidity was derived through latent class analysis of disease combinations. The primary outcome was change in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) from admission to discharge, calculated using the Berlin Initiative Study 1 (BIS1) equation. A relative decline was defined as ≥ 20% reduction from baseline. Multivariable models were adjusted for age, sex, baseline eGFR, acute diagnoses, and number of medications. Among 6,755 patients (mean age 80.6 years; 47% women), multimorbidity prevalence ranged from 87 to 93%. Quantitative multimorbidity showed modest and inconsistent associations with renal decline. In contrast, qualitative multimorbidity consistently predicted eGFR deterioration. Across all cohorts, the cardiorespiratory and renal cluster was associated with higher odds of in-hospital eGFR decline compared with neurogeriatric and mixed patterns (geriatrics OR 2.24 [95% CI 1.16-4.70]; internal medicine OR 1.72 [95% CI 1.22-2.45]; nephrology OR 2.11 [95% CI 1.01-4.56]). Disease-pattern-based multimorbidity better stratifies short-term renal risk than disease counts, identifying high-risk patients for targeted nephroprotective care during hospitalization.

articles.title: Dietary sodium density as a potential nutritional marker of HSI-defined hepatic steatosis in Korean adults: a nationwide cross-sectional study with a dose-response analysis.
articles.abstract: The association between energy-adjusted dietary sodium density and non-invasively assessed hepatic steatosis remains poorly defined in population-based studies. We investigated the association and dose-response relationship between dietary sodium density and HSI-defined hepatic steatosis in Korean adults. We analyzed 14,445 adults (aged ≥20 years) from the 2021-2023 KNHANES. Sodium intake from a 24-h recall was calculated as sodium density (mg/1,000 kcal). HSI ≥36 defined hepatic steatosis; descriptive analyses compared HSI <36 versus ≥36, whereas regression analyses used HSI <30 as the reference, with HSI 30.0-35.9 treated separately. Compared with HSI <30, each 100 mg/1,000 kcal increase in sodium density was associated with higher odds of HSI-defined hepatic steatosis across all models: Unadjusted OR 1.058 (95% CI 1.032-1.085; P<0.001), Age/Sex-adjusted OR 1.051 (95% CI 1.024-1.079; P<0.001), Lifestyle-adjusted OR 1.048 (95% CI 1.020-1.077; P=0.001), and Fully adjusted OR 1.054 (95% CI 1.020-1.089; P=0.002). Participants in the highest sodium density quartile (Q4) exhibited 36.2% higher odds of HSI-defined hepatic steatosis than those in the lowest quartile (Q1) (adjusted OR 1.362; 95% CI 1.144-1.621; P=0.0004; P for trend = 0.001). The association remained robust after adjusting for potassium density (OR 1.042; 95% CI 1.012-1.072; P=0.005). RCS analysis showed an approximately linear increase in odds across the observed range, without evidence of non-linearity (P=0.738). Elevated sodium density was associated with higher odds of HSI-defined hepatic steatosis and may serve as a nutritional marker of metabolic liver health.

articles.title: The challenges and opportunities of major trauma care in Germany - results of multidisciplinary expert interviews of the LeAf trauma study.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: The recovery process of major trauma survivors involves various sectors within a complex system of different medical service providers and stakeholders who accompany and support patients throughout the recovery pathway. The aim was to explore experiences and opinions of experts, who are actively involved in the care of major trauma patients in the German healthcare system. Semistructured in-depth group interviews were used to investigate experiences and opinions of experts with the focus on exploration of expert perspectives on opportunities and challenges of the cross sectoral care. An exploratory analysis was performed with an artificial intelligence-based coding software. In a second step, a system map was developed, and all inter- and intra-sectoral challenges and all opportunities for the optimization of processes were mapped. 39 experts from 13 medical specialties and occupational groups who were interviewed highlighted that intersectional issues especially across and within sectors pose a significant challenge to patient care. Four challenges were highlighted that significantly influence patient care: (1) Communication between sectors; (2) Complexity of transitions between sectors; (3) Inadequate aftercare and (4) Lack of psychosocial care. In conclusion five key learnings can be derived which could help to transform the healthcare system towards a system in which the complex condition major trauma with its high potential of chronification is enabling patients towards living a self-determined life and is creating opportunities for patients to return to work: (1) interdisciplinary collaboration (2), improved communication (3), early psychosocial screening and intervention (4), continuity of care (5), involvement of relatives.

articles.title: Peri-periprosthetic femoral fractures: a single-centre case series of a rare and challenging clinical scenario.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Periprosthetic femoral fractures (PFFs) are an increasingly common complication of hip arthroplasty. A poorly defined scenario is a new femoral fracture after a previously treated PFF has united, which we term a peri-periprosthetic femoral fracture. We retrospectively reviewed 154 surgically treated PFF episodes in patients aged over 65 years at our institution between 2011 and 2021. A peri-periprosthetic fracture was defined as a new acute femoral fracture after documented radiographic union of a previously treated PFF. Clinical, surgical, and radiographic data were reviewed. Seven patients (4.5% of the institutional PFF cohort) met the criteria. Mean age was 83.1 years and 6 (85.7%) were female. The mean interval to the peri-periprosthetic fracture was 37.3 months (median 27; range 7-105). By the Vancouver classification, 3 fractures were type B1, 1 type B3, and 3 type C. Treatment was individualised to fracture configuration, prosthetic stability, hardware, and bone stock. Radiographic union was documented in all 4 patients with adequate follow-up, at a mean of 4.3 months. Five patients regained ambulation; one with pre-existing limitations did not, and ambulatory status was unavailable for one. Medical complications occurred in 2 patients, and no major orthopaedic complication required reoperation. Mortality was 14.3% at one year and 42.9% at two years. Peri-periprosthetic femoral fractures constitute a rare and technically demanding scenario, distinct from delayed union, nonunion, refracture through an incompletely healed fracture, and fixation failure. Treatment should be individualised to prosthetic stability, pre-existing hardware, fracture morphology, and residual bone stock.

articles.title: In-hospital mortality in hip fracture patients undergoing surgery later than 24 hours post admission might rather reflect the impact of comorbidities and treatment limitations than additional risks imposed by the mere timely delay itself.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Early surgery for proximal femoral fractures is widely recommended, but the association between surgical delay and short-term mortality remains uncertain because observational studies are vulnerable to confounding by patient characteristics and treatment limitation. We retrospectively studied adults with operatively treated proximal femoral fractures at a DGU-certified regional trauma center in Germany (2022-2025). Time to surgery was measured from emergency department registration to operative start. Delays > 24 h were classified as medical or non-medical where sufficiently documented. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Adjusted analyses included age, sex, ASA category, fracture type, concomitant orthopaedic injury, and treatment limitation (DNR/DNI; not time-anchored to surgery) and used Firth penalized logistic regression. Among 927 patients, 871 (94.0%) underwent surgery within 24 h; 53 (5.7%) died in hospital. Crude mortality was 5.6% after surgery within 24 h and 7.1% after surgery > 24 h. After adjustment, no clear independent association between surgery > 24 h and mortality was detected (aOR 1.03, 95% CI 0.29-2.92). Higher age, male sex, advanced ASA class, and treatment limitation were associated with mortality. In exploratory analyses, mortality was 19.0% among medically delayed patients and 0% among patients with non-medical delay, but adjusted estimates were highly imprecise. No clear association between surgery beyond 24 h and in-hospital mortality was detected after adjustment for measured patient characteristics and treatment-limitation status. The estimate was imprecise and compatible with clinically relevant benefit or harm; these findings do not establish the absence of an effect of surgical delay.

articles.title: Reporting of Sociodemographic and Equity-Related Factors in Emergency Department Pain Trials for Children: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract: Effective management of children's acute pain in emergency departments (EDs) is essential, yet health disparities exist. The applicability of evidence to diverse pediatric populations depends on clear demographic reporting. The PROGRESS-Plus framework identifies social determinants of health that influence care and outcomes, but it is unclear to what extent randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in pediatric ED pain management report these variables. This scoping review examines the frequency and completeness of PROGRESS-Plus reporting in RCTs evaluating acute pain interventions for children in EDs in Canada and the USA. Using Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and the Participant, Concept, Context framework, we conducted a scoping review of RCTs published between 2013 and 2025. MEDLINE, PsycINFO, CINAHL, and CENTRAL were searched using a peer-reviewed strategy. Eligible studies involved children and youth experiencing acute presenting or procedural pain in ED settings. Two reviewers independently screened studies. Data were extracted using standardized forms refined with input from patient partners. Narrative synthesis and descriptive statistics were applied to summarize PROGRESS-Plus reporting. Of 3667 records identified, 65 RCTs met inclusion criteria. Thirty-five studies focused on procedural pain interventions, and 30 on interventions for painful presentations. Age was reported in all studies, and gender and/or sex in 98%. Race and/or ethnicity was reported in 40%, and chronic illness and/or disability in 18%. No studies reported socioeconomic status or place of residence. RCTs addressing pediatric pain in the ED rarely report equity-relevant demographic variables beyond age and gender and/or sex, limiting assessment of intervention effectiveness across diverse populations. Standardized demographic reporting is needed to support equitable, evidence-based pain research and care.

articles.title: Prehospital Minithoracostomy versus Chest Drainage for Emergency Pleural Decompression in Major Trauma.
articles.abstract: Prehospital pleural decompression is life-saving in patients with suspected tension pneumothorax or other life-threatening thoracic pressure pathology after major trauma. Although prehospital minithoracostomy (PHMT) is increasingly adopted by physician-led helicopter emergency medical services (HEMS), comparative evidence with prehospital chest drainage (PHCD) remains limited. We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study of consecutive adult trauma patients undergoing prehospital pleural decompression within a physician-led HEMS between January 2018 and December 2024, managed with PHMT or PHCD according to clinical judgment. The primary outcome, scene time, was analyzed using Bayesian robust Student-t regression; recorded complications and survival were analyzed using Bayesian beta-binomial models, with posterior risk differences and credible intervals. Ninety-four patients were included (66 PHMT; 28 PHCD). After excluding two implausible zero-minute scene-time records, the posterior median difference in scene time was -5.9 min (95% credible interval [CrI], -13.8 to 1.7; 94.0% probability PHMT was shorter). Complication status was evaluable in 50/66 PHMT and 10/28 PHCD patients. Recorded complications occurred in 0/50 evaluable PHMT and 6/10 evaluable PHCD patients (risk difference -58.7 percentage points, 95% CrI -83.9 to -29.3; probability >99.9% that recorded complications were less frequent with PHMT). Prehospital survival was lower with PHMT, reflecting greater baseline severity, whereas no clear differences were observed at 1, 30, or 90 days. Prehospital minithoracostomy was not associated with longer scene time and was associated with fewer recorded complications than PHCD. Because allocation was nonrandomized, complication ascertainment differed between procedures, and few events occurred, these findings are hypothesis-generating rather than evidence of comparative safety. Prospective multicenter studies with standardized indications and systematic outcome assessment are warranted.
